children: Boot Barn Holdings posted higher profit and revenue on an uptick in same store sales while at the same time lowering its full-year guidance.
The footwear retailer on Wednesday posted a second-quarter profit of $52.5 million, or $1.73 a share, compared with $42.2 million, or $1.37 a share, a year earlier.
Revenue increased 15% to $581.8 million. Analysts polled by FactSet expected $580.8 million.
The company said consolidated same store sales increased 1.4%, retail store same store sales increased 1% and e-commerce same store sales increased 5.2%

For the current fiscal year Boot Barn lowered its revenue guidance to $2.57 billion to $2.59 billion, from $2.58 billion to $2.63 billion. Consolidated same store sales growth is now forecasted to rise 0.8% to 2%, down from 2% to 4% previously.
Analysts polled by FactSet expect revenue at $2.6 billion and a 3.1% increase in same store sales.
Net income is now seen at $263.6 million to $272 million, down from $267.9 million to $281.0 million before earnings were released.
The forecast for earnings per share was sliced to $8.72 to $9, down from $8.80 to $9.23.
Wall Street analysts expect a profit of $277 million and earnings per share of $9.04
While Boot Barn cuts its outlook it increased the number of stores it expects to open in the current fiscal year 75 to 80 locations, up from 70 previously.
Boot Barn authorized an additional $400 million of its shares to be repurchased under its existing buyback program, leaving $468 million available for future share repurchases.

For the current quarter sales are forecasted at $785 million to $802 million, and earnings per share of $3.03 to $3.19. Wall Street analysts expect $816.2 million of sales and per share earnings of $3.39.
The company also approved spending an additional $400 million to purchase its shares as part of its existing buyback program, leaving $468 million available for future share buybacks.
